recentItems.title: US envoys prepare for Ukraine talks after meeting Russia’s Vladimir Putin | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Two US envoys are hoping for "equally productive meetings" in Ukraine after holding talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on ending the war, US officials say.
 
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to land in Kyiv on Sunday, the first trip by US President Donald Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital. 
 
They discussed "substantive plans for next steps" with Putin on Saturday according to the White House, and an announcement is expected in the coming weeks, as efforts to end the war in Ukraine gather pace.
 
Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was ready for "a substantive conversation" as Witkoff and Kushner were negotiating at the Kremlin, with talks lasting three hours in Putin's official residence on Saturday.

recentItems.title: Why The Witcher 3’s new expansion almost didn't happen | BBC News
recentItems.description:
When CD Projekt Red announced it was making a new expansion for the hugely popular action-role playing game The Witcher 3, it came as a shock.
 
The original, after all, came out 11 years ago.
 
BBC Tech Now's Laura Cress spoke to the team behind the Songs of the Past expansion, as well as finding out why it's happening now.

recentItems.title: How damaging is Reform’s donation row? | BBC Newscast
recentItems.description:
Nigel Farage has said he "frankly wasn't listening" during a conversation with his former chief of staff and an undercover reporter discussing what appears to have been a scheme to funnel foreign money to Reform UK.

The row has overshadowed the party’s conference in Birmingham, where Laura Kuenssberg, Chris Mason, and Joe Pike got together to discuss Farage’s response and the policies coming from the event.

Why have two Reform UK officials stood down after an undercover investigation? | BBC Newscast
recentItems.description:
Two senior officials stood down from Reform UK after a Channel 4 News report prompted the party to investigate claims about funding.  

Nigel Farage's senior aide Dan Jukes and Reform's head of policy James Orr have both stood down pending the outcome of the internal probe. The undercover filming was done by Verbatim Investigations and broadcast by Channel 4 News. Reform UK has denied wrongdoing and Nigel Farage describes the operation as entrapment.  

The footage appears to show an attempt to secure funding from someone they believed to be a foreign donor. Electoral law prohibits UK political parties from receiving financial contributions from people who can't vote here.  Reform denies any wrongdoing and says it has "been the target of a hoax perpetuated by foreign-funded climate change activists". Adam and Chris discuss.

recentItems.title: Port of Dover disruption as masked 'stop the boats' protesters block roads | BBC News
recentItems.description:
There has been major disruption at the Port of Dover, the UK's biggest international ferry port.
 
Masked protesters who were blocking access were chanting "stop the boats".
 
Ferry operators said they are aware of the "traffic disruption" and would accommodate passengers on the next departure once they arrive.
 
The UK government said: "The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but we condemn the behaviour in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused."
